'''Jeremy Bulloch''' (16 February 1945 – 17 December 2020) was an English actor. He played [[Boba Fett]], inside the costume and armor, in ''The Empire Strikes Back'' (1980) and ''Return of the Jedi'' (1983).<ref name="swcom">[https://www.starwars.com/news/jeremy-bulloch Boba Fett Performer Jeremy Bulloch Passes Away], StarWars.com (17 December 2020). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20260914104329/https://www.starwars.com/news/jeremy-bulloch Internet Archive]</ref><ref name="bbc">[https://www.bbc.com/news/entertainment-arts-55358301 Star Wars' Boba Fett actor Jeremy Bulloch dies aged 75], BBC News (17 December 2020). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20260212020831/https://www.bbc.com/news/entertainment-arts-55358301 Internet Archive]</ref><ref name="wp-jb">[https://starwars.fandom.com/wiki/Jeremy_Bulloch Jeremy Bulloch], Wookieepedia. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20251207202112/https://starwars.fandom.com/wiki/Jeremy_Bulloch Internet Archive]</ref> In ''The Empire Strikes Back'' he also played the Imperial officer who appears in SWCCG as [[Lieutenant Sheckil]].<ref name="swcom" /><ref name="wp-sheckil">[https://starwars.fandom.com/wiki/Sheckil Sheckil], Wookieepedia. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20251210113330/https://starwars.fandom.com/wiki/Sheckil Internet Archive]</ref> He was a special guest at [[DecipherCon 1999]], billed as Boba Fett from the Star Wars films. He signed photographs with [[Shannon Baksa]] (Mara Jade).<ref name="fri27">[https://web.archive.org/web/20000610080211/http://www.decipher.com/calendars/event/mainevents/deciphercon/photos/FRI/fri27.html DecipherCon 1999 Friday photo fri27], Decipher (Wayback 10 June 2000). Caption: "Celebrity guest Jeremy Bulloch, 'Boba Fett' from the Star Wars trilogy, stands tall as Shannon Baksa, Decipher's Mara Jade, signs photos for fans"</ref><ref name="guests">[https://web.archive.org/web/20000122135443/http://decipher.com/calendars/event/mainevents/deciphercon/specialguests/index.html Special guests], DecipherCon '99 (Wayback 22 January 2000)</ref> ''Star Wars Insider'' quoted him there: "It's a real pleasure to be here."<ref name="insider48" />

== Star Wars roles ==
Bulloch's half-brother Robert Watts, associate producer of ''The Empire Strikes Back'', offered him the Boba Fett part on the condition that the costume fit him.<ref name="swcom" /> Bulloch said he played the bounty hunter as "Clint Eastwood in a suit of armor".<ref name="swcom" /> He gave the physical performance; in the original releases Boba Fett's voice was Jason Wingreen's.<ref name="wp-jb" />

Bulloch also appeared without a helmet in the Cloud City scenes of ''The Empire Strikes Back''. He played the Imperial officer who escorts the captive Princess Leia toward Darth Vader's ship. He took the part on the day of shooting because the actor cast as the officer was unavailable.<ref name="swcom" /><ref name="wp-sheckil-legends">[https://starwars.fandom.com/wiki/Sheckil/Legends Sheckil (Legends)], Wookieepedia. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20251127094637/https://starwars.fandom.com/wiki/Sheckil/Legends Internet Archive]</ref> The film does not name the officer. Decipher named him Lieutenant Sheckil in [[Cloud City Limited]] (November 1997), and ''Star Wars: Force Collection'' later used the name in canon.<ref name="wp-sheckil" /><ref name="wp-sheckil-legends" />

In ''Revenge of the Sith'' (2005) Bulloch played Captain Colton, the captain of the ''Tantive III''.<ref name="swcom" /> He died on 17 December 2020, aged 75.<ref name="bbc" />

== Lore wordplay ==
The lore of [[Lieutenant Sheckil]] reads:

<blockquote>Former warrant officer from Concord Dawn. Promoted due to superb performance. Specializes in transporting high-profile criminals. Twin brother of a famous mercenary.<ref name="card-sheckil">[[Lieutenant Sheckil]], [[Cloud City Limited]] (Decipher, November 1997), card lore and game text. [[:File:CC-D-lieutenantsheckil.gif]]</ref></blockquote>

The same actor played Sheckil and the bounty hunter Boba Fett in ''The Empire Strikes Back''.<ref name="swcom" /> When the card was released, Concord Dawn was also Boba Fett's home, from the 1996 story "The Last One Standing: The Tale of Boba Fett". ''Attack of the Clones'' (2002) later made Fett a clone born on Kamino.<ref name="wp-sheckil-legends" /> In the film, Boba Fett has Han Solo loaded aboard his ship, ''Slave I'', with the line "Put Captain Solo in the cargo hold."<ref name="wp-jb" /> Wookieepedia's Sheckil article calls the Concord Dawn and twin-brother details tongue-in-cheek references to Bulloch playing Boba Fett.<ref name="wp-sheckil-legends" />

[[Human Shield]] is tied to Sheckil in play and in its art. Sheckil's game text reads "During your control phase, may use 1 Force to search your Reserve Deck, take one Human Shield into hand and reshuffle. When escorting a captive, captive is forfeit +2 and Sheckil is immune to attrition < 4."<ref name="card-sheckil" /> Human Shield's image is the Cloud City shot of Sheckil holding Leia in front of him, and its lore reads "A shining example of Imperial honor and bravery."<ref name="card-hs">[[Human Shield]], [[Cloud City Limited]] (Decipher, November 1997), card lore and image. [[:File:CloudCity-D-humanshield-decipher-archive.gif]]</ref>

Lucasfilm's Pablo Hidalgo joked about the character's relatives in a 2004 ''Revenge of the Sith'' set diary. Noting that Bulloch had played Sheckil and would play the ''Tantive'' pilot, he wrote: "Makes you wonder if Sheckil has an Alderaanian relative."<ref name="wp-sheckil-legends" />
